    CPU and RAM health¶

    Does a scope's board compute correctly, keep its full speed and stay cool under a sustained full load? This notebook reads one standard one-hour run per scope, gives each board a verdict, and compares processor and memory speed across the fleet.

    Analysis written by Claude (Anthropic); conceptualised and verified by Yatharth Bhasin.

    Protocol¶

    Acquisition: scripts/debug/cpu_ram_health.py, protocol cpu_ram_health/2. install_requirements() once per scope (stress-ng, sysbench and smartmontools, with apt), then create_exp() and start(). No acquisition may run at the same time. About 2 h 8 min per scope:

    1. Settle, 60 s idle. Refused if anything else uses more than 10% of the CPU.
    2. Speed, sysbench, 3 × 20 s each: CPU on 1 and on 4 threads; RAM write and read on 4 threads with 16 MiB blocks, larger than the 1 MiB L2 cache, so the RAM is measured and not the cache.
    3. Stress, stress-ng, 120 min: 4 CPU workers cycling through every CPU method, plus 1 memory worker cycling through every memory pattern on a fixed 5 GiB. Every result is checked against the known answer (--verify).
    4. Cooldown, 2 min idle.

    Clock, throttle flags, SoC temperature, fan, memory and swap are logged once a second throughout, the SSD's own temperature sensor once a minute (the test puts no load on the SSD, so any rise is heat from the board), and the kernel log is kept. The parameters are fixed in the script; a run with any of them changed is marked non-standard. Protocol /1 had a 60 min stress phase and no SSD temperature; both versions can be read here.

    Data¶

    Runs are read with trappy-explorer's legacy reader, explorer.legacy.ExpExplorer. Only folders with KIND in their name are used, so DATA may hold other runs too. One row per run. The speed stream has one row per sysbench repeat (test, unit, repeat, value).

    Each run folder also holds:

    • health.yaml: the board's identity and set-up (serial, kernel, firmware, bootloader, config.txt values, tool versions), the speed results, the stress-ng exit code and metrics, the kernel check, and the verdict the script gave on the scope.
    • <eid>_telemetry.csv: one row per second: phase, arm_mhz, throttled, soc_temp_c, fan, busy_pct, load1, mem_avail_mib, swap_used_mib, ssd_temp_c. arm_mhz and throttled are read every 5 s and ssd_temp_c every 60 s (protocol /2 only); they are blank in between.
    • kernel.log, and in raw/ the stress-ng log and YAML, every sysbench output and the scope's config.txt.

    Files are looked up by name anywhere inside the run folder.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    def find(d, pattern):
    hit = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "**", pattern), recursive=True))
    return hit[0] if hit else None

def telemetry(d):
    t = pd.read_csv(find(d, "*_telemetry.csv"))
    t["minutes"] = (t.wall - t.wall.iloc[0]) / 60
    t["throttled"] = [int(v, 16) if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("0x") else np.nan
                      for v in t.throttled]
    t["fan"] = pd.to_numeric(t.fan, errors="coerce")
    t["ssd_temp_c"] = pd.to_numeric(t.get("ssd_temp_c"), errors="coerce")   # absent before /2
    return t

H = {k: yaml.safe_load(open(find(r.dir, "health.yaml"))) for k, r in runs.iterrows()}
T = {k: telemetry(r.dir) for k, r in runs.iterrows()}
pd.DataFrame({k: t.groupby("phase", sort=False).size() for k, t in T.items()}).T.rename_axis(
    ["scope", "run"])                                     # seconds of telemetry per phase

    Boards¶

    What each board is and how it is set up. Identical boards should show the same kernel, firmware and bootloader. A scope that differs here is the first place to look when its numbers differ below.

    def board(h):
    s = h["system"]
    return {"model": s["model"].replace("Raspberry Pi ", "Pi "), "revision": s["revision"],
            "serial": s["serial"], "kernel": s["kernel"].split("+")[0],
            "firmware": " ".join(s["firmware"].split()[:3]), "bootloader": s["bootloader"].split()[0],
            "arm_freq": s["arm_freq"], "over_voltage": s["over_voltage"], "fans": s["fans"],
            "swap_mib": s["swap_total_mib"], "stress_ng": s["stress_ng"].split()[2].rstrip(","),
            "sysbench": s["sysbench"].split()[-1], "protocol": h["protocol"], "standard": h["standard"]}

pd.DataFrame([{"scope": k[0], "run": k[1], **board(h)} for k, h in H.items()]).set_index(["scope", "run"])

    Speed¶

    Each test's result as a percentage of the fleet median (the median over scopes of each scope's median), one point per repeat. Identical boards sit within a few percent of zero. A scope below zero in every repeat is slower; repeats far apart from each other point to something else running during the test. The table gives each scope's median in the test's own unit (events/s for CPU, MiB/s for RAM).

    Temperature through the run¶

    SoC temperature (30 s mean) against time since the start of each run: the speed tests in the first minutes, the hour of stress, then the cooldown. The curve should rise, settle to a plateau and fall back at the end. The Pi 4 starts slowing itself down at 80 °C. A plateau that keeps climbing, or one far above the other scopes' at the same room temperature, points to the cooling: fan, heatsink or airflow.

    Cooling¶

    Left: the plateau, the mean SoC temperature over the last 10 min of stress, above the room temperature read by the scope's T&H sensor at the start and end, so that scopes in warmer or cooler spots compare. Right: how fast the board cools once the load stops: the time constant τ of an exponential fitted to the cooldown, decaying towards the board's idle temperature before the run. τ is the time it takes to lose 63% of the excess heat; a smaller τ is better cooling.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    decay = lambda x, a, tau, c: c + a * np.exp(-x / tau)

def cooling(k, t):
    st, cd, idle = (t[t.phase == p] for p in ("stress", "cooldown", "settle"))
    room = [x["temp_c"] for x in (H[k]["system"].get("tandh_start"), H[k]["system"].get("tandh_end")) if x]
    plateau, c = st.soc_temp_c.tail(600).mean(), idle.soc_temp_c.mean()
    x, y = cd.elapsed_s - cd.elapsed_s.iloc[0], cd.soc_temp_c
    try:
        (a, tau), _ = curve_fit(lambda x, a, tau: decay(x, a, tau, c), x, y,
                                p0=(y.iloc[0] - c, 60), bounds=([0, 1], [100, 5000]))
    except (RuntimeError, ValueError):
        tau = np.nan
    return {"room_c": np.mean(room) if room else np.nan, "plateau_c": plateau,
            "rise_c": plateau - np.mean(room) if room else np.nan, "cooldown_tau_s": tau,
            "fan_on_pct": 100 * (st.fan > 0).mean() if st.fan.notna().any() else np.nan}

cool = pd.DataFrame([{"scope": k[0], "run": k[1], **cooling(k, t)} for k, t in T.items()]).set_index(["scope", "run"])

for ax, col, label in zip(axes, ["rise_c", "cooldown_tau_s"],
                          ["plateau above room (°C)", "cooldown time constant τ (s)"]):

    Clock under load¶

    Every clock reading during the stress phase. A healthy board holds its configured clock (arm_freq) the whole time. Readings below it mean the firmware capped or throttled the clock, for heat or for a low supply voltage; the throttle flags in the results say which.

    Memory¶

    Available memory and swap in use through the run. The memory worker holds a fixed 5 GiB during the stress phase, so available memory drops by about that much and comes back at the end. Some swap while plenty of memory is still available is normal Linux behaviour under this load. Swap that keeps growing, or available memory near zero, means something else holds memory.

    SSD temperature¶

    The SSD's own temperature sensor, read once a minute, against time since the start of each run. The test puts no load on the drive, so a rise is heat from the board next to it. Some drives report a fixed value instead of a live reading; a flat line that never moves, at the same value on every drive of that model, is one of those. Runs recorded before protocol /2 have no SSD temperature.

    In [13]:
    Copied!

    for (s, run), t in have_ssd.items():
        ax.plot(t.minutes, t.ssd_temp_c, color=COLORS[s], alpha=1 / run, marker=".",
                label=s if run == 1 else None)
    ax.set_xlabel("minutes since the start of the run")
    ax.set_ylabel("SSD temperature (°C)")
    ax.legend(ncol=len(have_ssd), loc="lower center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0))
    fig.tight_layout()
else:
    print("No SSD temperature in these runs.")

def ssd(k, t):
    v, st = t.ssd_temp_c.dropna(), t[t.phase == "stress"]
    if v.empty:
        return {"ssd_model": H[k].get("ssd", {}).get("model")}
    last = st[st.wall >= st.wall.max() - 600].ssd_temp_c.dropna()
    return {"ssd_model": H[k].get("ssd", {}).get("model"), "ssd_start_c": v.iloc[0],
            "ssd_plateau_c": last.mean(), "ssd_rise_c": last.mean() - v.iloc[0],
            "ssd_max_c": v.max(), "ssd_constant": v.nunique() == 1}

ssd_tab = pd.DataFrame([{"scope": k[0], "run": k[1], **ssd(k, t)} for k, t in T.items()]).set_index(["scope", "run"])
ssd_tab.round(1)

    Results¶

    One row per run, also written next to each run's data (analysis/cpu_ram_health.yaml) and exported to results/. wrong_results: stress-ng log lines reporting a wrong result. kernel_faults: kernel errors during the run (oops, segfault, lockup, RCU stall, SError); blank if the kernel log was not captured. throttle_during: throttle flags raised during the run, or none. ssd_*: the SSD temperature summary from above. clock_held_pct: share of stress-phase clock readings at arm_freq. *_pct: speed against the fleet median. verdict follows the acceptance table below; script_verdict is what the script recorded on the scope.

    In [14]:
    Copied! 
    NAMES = ["under-voltage", "frequency capped", "throttled", "soft temperature limit"]

def flags(t):
    """Throttle flags raised during the run: 'now' bits, and 'since boot' bits not set at the start."""
    v = t.throttled.dropna().astype(int).to_numpy()
    if not len(v):
        return "unknown"
    seen = np.bitwise_or.reduce(v)
    during = (seen & 0xF) | ((seen >> 16) & 0xF & ~(v[0] >> 16 & 0xF))
    return ", ".join(n for i, n in enumerate(NAMES) if during >> i & 1) or "none"

def row(k, r):
    h, t, s = H[k], T[k], H[k].get("stress") or {}
    st, arm = t[t.phase == "stress"], h["system"]["arm_freq"]
    log = find(r.dir, "stress-ng.log")
    kern = h.get("kernel", {})
    return {"scope": k[0], "run": k[1], "eid": r.eid, "serial": h["system"]["serial"],
            "standard": h["standard"], "stress_exit": s.get("exit_code"),
            "complete": not h["stopped_early"] and s.get("ran_s", 0) >= 0.95 * s.get("planned_s", 1),
            "wrong_results": sum(bool(re.search(r"\bfail:", l)) for l in open(log)) if log else np.nan,
            "kernel_faults": len(kern["faults"]) if kern.get("captured") else np.nan,
            "oom": len(kern.get("oom", [])), "throttle_during": flags(t),
            "clock_held_pct": 100 * (st.arm_mhz.dropna() >= 0.99 * arm).mean(),
            "soc_max_c": st.soc_temp_c.max(), "swap_max_mib": t.swap_used_mib.max(),
            "script_verdict": h.get("verdict")}

speed = sp.groupby(["eid", "test"]).value.median().unstack()[list(TESTS)]
speed_pct = (100 * (speed / fleet_med[list(TESTS)] - 1)).add_suffix("_pct")
fleet = pd.DataFrame([row(k, r) for k, r in runs.iterrows()]).set_index(["scope", "run"])
fleet = fleet.join(cool).join(ssd_tab).join(speed_pct, on="eid")

    Acceptance¶

    Per board:

    Criterion Level
    stress-ng reports a wrong result (exit 2, or a fail: line in its log) FAIL
    A kernel error during the run FAIL
    The run stopped early, stress-ng exited with another error, memory ran out, or a speed test gave no result INCOMPLETE
    Under-voltage during the run WARN: check the power supply and cable before the board
    Clock capped or throttled, or below arm_freq in more than 1% of the stress-phase readings WARN
    SoC at 80 °C or more WARN
    Kernel log not captured WARN

    FAIL means a board fault: replace the board, or rerun to confirm. INCOMPLETE means rerun. Speed is not judged; it is compared across the fleet. Swap is reported but not judged: holding 5 GiB makes the kernel swap briefly on healthy boards too. The script counted swap as a WARN in protocol /1, so for those runs script_verdict can say WARN where verdict says PASS. SSD temperature is reported, not judged.

    Persistent records¶

    This calibration writes 0 records to the scope. Its set-up step, install_requirements(), installs stress-ng and sysbench with apt; nothing else on the scope changes.
